Security Guard Training

Concept preparation for security guard work: the limits of a guard's authority, observe-and-report, writing reports that hold up, and verbal de-escalation.

1

2

Outcomes

About This Program

The central lesson of this coursework is the gap between instinct and authority. A guard's powers are generally those of a private citizen, so the response that feels right during an incident is frequently the one that creates legal exposure and personal risk. The job is deterrence, accurate observation, and reporting — and a report written in conclusions rather than observations is worth very little when it is read eighteen months later by someone looking for weaknesses.

By the end of this program you can

  • ✓Describe the guard's role and how their authority differs from a police officer's
  • ✓Explain the personal legal exposure created by exceeding that authority
  • ✓Apply observe-and-report to an incident in progress
  • ✓Record a description with the specifics a report needs
  • ✓Write an incident report covering who, what, when, where, how, and action taken
  • ✓Distinguish an observation from a conclusion, and write only the first
  • ✓Apply verbal de-escalation techniques
  • ✓Recognize that suspicion must rest on describable behavior, not appearance

Related Certifications

    NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services (training schools approved by DCJS)
    8-hour pre-assignment course before applying, 16-hour on-the-job training within 90 days, and an 8-hour in-service course every year. Registration lasts two years.
  • State licensure elsewhere
    Individual state licensing authorities
    Requirements vary widely; check the state you will work in.

What This Coursework Is

IMPORTANT — this coursework is not a license and does not satisfy any state training requirement. In New York, a security guard completes an 8-hour pre-assignment course at a school approved by the Division of Criminal Justice Services (DCJS) before applying, registers with the NYS Department of State, Division of Licensing Services, completes 16 hours of on-the-job training within 90 days of starting work, and takes an 8-hour in-service course every year. Armed guard work also requires a New York pistol license, a 47-hour firearms course, and annual firearms training. Other states have their own requirements. No online course from a non-approved provider satisfies these, and this one does not claim to. Use it to arrive at approved training already understanding the material. Nothing here is legal advice — authority, use of force, and citizen's arrest are defined by state law and vary considerably.
